findings.heading: DAGs
findings.proposition: The Portuguese section title expands DAG as "Graficos ciclicos direcionados" (directed CYCLIC graphs); the English "DAGs" and the linked ggdag/dagitty material define a DAG as a directed ACYCLIC graph.
findings.reader_consequence: A Portuguese reader learns the defining property of a DAG backwards: acyclicity is the whole point of the structure used for causal inference, so the reader may believe cycles are permitted and misread every DAG example and the linked vignettes.

findings.heading: Import data
findings.proposition: The Portuguese says "Para ver as primeiras 50 linhas do banco utilize o codigo a seguir" (to see the first 50 rows, use the code that follows); the English says the first 50 rows ARE displayed below, and the chunk that follows is set echo=F so no code is shown to the reader, only the rendered table.
findings.reader_consequence: The reader looks for code to copy and run, but the chunk is hidden by echo=F and only an interactive table appears, so the instruction cannot be carried out as written.

findings.heading: Syntax
findings.proposition: The Portuguese glosses the node attribute `sides` as "Tamanhos" (sizes); the English gives no gloss, and `sides` in Graphviz sets the number of sides of a polygon shape, not any size.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader wanting to change node size reaches for `sides`, gets a polygon with a different number of edges instead, and never finds the actual size attributes `height`, `width` and `fixedsize` listed two lines below.

findings.heading: Syntax
findings.proposition: The Portuguese glosses the node attribute `peripheries` as "Margens" (margins); the English gives no gloss, and `peripheries` in Graphviz sets the number of outlines drawn around the node shape, while margin spacing is the separate `margin` attribute.
findings.reader_consequence: A reader wanting to change padding inside or around a node sets `peripheries` and gets extra concentric outlines drawn on the shape instead.
